Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment
.

1. This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 25.01.2024 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.-II, Yadgiri, [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.245/2020 seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.-II, Yadgiri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The injured claimant, met with an accident on 06.08.2020 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, he filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking NC: 2025:KHC-K:6795 HC-KAR compensation of Rs.62,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record,
awarded the compensation of Rs.3,19,700/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant-claimant has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has contended that Tribunal has awarded meagre compensation under all heads.
It is contended that claimant sustained grievous injuries and

sentences.text: 2 support of it he got examined the Doctor as PW2, who assessed 21% disability in relation to lower limb, but the Tribunal has taken only 10% disability.

It is also contended that though the claimant was working as Coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, the Tribunal has taken notional income at Rs.12,000/- per month and thus, requested for NC: 2025:KHC-K:6795 HC-KAR enhancing the compensation with 12% interest per annum instead of 6%.
5.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.
6. PW2 - Doctor, the claimant has sustained United Proximal Tibia Fracture of Left Side with permanent physical impairment in relation to lower limb at 21% disability.
The Tribunal considering the same, has rightly assessed 10% functional disability, which needs no interference.
7. The claimant stated that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but failed to produced any document to prove the same.

As the accident is of the year 2020, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, this Court deems it appropriate to reassess the income of the claimant at NC: 2025:KHC-K:6795 HC-KAR Rs.13,750/- per month.
At the time of accident, the claimant was aged 57 years as per his Aadhaar Card and appropriate multiplier applicable to his age group is '9'.

Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for loss of future earning as under:
Rs.13,750/- x 12 x 9 x 10% = Rs.1,48,500/-
8.
The claimant was admitted in the hospital for 6 days.
Considering the age of the claimant, nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities.

Further, due to injuries the claimant might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 3 months, hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.41,250/- for loss of income during laid up period.

However, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads i.e., for medical expenses at Rs.20,399/-, for pain and suffering at Rs.50,000/-, for food and nourishment charges at Rs.10,000/-, for Attendant charges at Rs.10,000/-, for transportation at Rs.10,000/- and for NC: 2025:KHC-K:6795 HC-KAR future medical expenses at Rs15,000/-
needs no interference.

9. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
Sl. Heads Award by the Award by this No. Tribunal Court 1 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/- Rs.50,000/- 2 Medical Expenses Rs.20,300/- Rs.20,300/- 3 Loss of future Rs.1,58,400/- Rs.1,48,500/-
earning capacity 4 Transportation, Rs.40,000/- Rs.40,000/-
extra nourishment and attendant charges 5 Loss of amenities -- Rs.25,000/- 6 Loss of income Rs.36,000/- Rs.41,250/-
during laid up period 7 Future medical Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
Hanumantha Rathod vs Mahadevappa And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40089445/
3 expenses Total Rs.3,19,700/- Rs.3,40,050/- There will be enhancement of Rs.20,350/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6795 HC-KAR 10.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has already deposited the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
 (ii) The claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.20,350/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

( iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment (iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
